elections.notes: Election for President of the Russian SFSR, then part of the Soviet Union. The article cites Nohlen & Stöver, the University of Essex and the FCI archive of the official count. Shares are of the table's valid votes, which include 1,525,410 votes against all candidates; 1,716,757 invalid ballots are excluded. Turnout is the infobox figure. No results by region in the article, so no region winners. The infobox gives Ryzhkov 13,359,335 votes; the results table's 13,395,335 is used.

source.name: Wikipedia, citing the Central Election Commission of Russia

elections.notes: Turnout is the run-off's (first round 69.67%), from the infobox. Shares are of the table's valid votes, which include votes against all candidates (1,163,921 in the first round, 3,604,462 in the run-off); invalid ballots are excluded. First-round Others: Svyatoslav Fyodorov, Mikhail Gorbachev, Martin Shakkum, Yury Vlasov, Vladimir Bryntsalov and Aman Tuleyev (308 early votes before he withdrew). The article cites Nohlen & Stöver, Colton and the CEC. Its results-by-subject tables are commented out of the page, so no region winners.

candidates.name: Communist Party of the Russian Federation
Party of Russian Unity and Accord

elections.notes: Seats are each party's total (225 party-list plus 225 constituency); votes and shares are the party-list vote. Shares include 2,267,963 party-list votes against all; 3,928,002 invalid ballots are excluded. Independents won only constituency seats, so they have no list votes. Independents won the most seats (135, flagged as winner); the largest party was the LDPR (64 seats and the most list votes). Six seats were vacant: five in Tatarstan (turnout under 25%) and one in Chechnya. No change column. The article cites Nohlen & Stöver, the University of Essex and Bochsler. Its by-region table is commented out of the page, so no region winners. The infobox's percentages are the CEC's, which also count invalid ballots (LDPR 21.35%).

elections.notes: Seats are each party's total (225 party-list plus 225 constituency); votes and shares are the party-list vote. The table counts 8 constituency seats under "Against all" (where that option won) and 1 vacant seat. Shares include 2,198,702 party-list votes against all; 1,296,992 invalid ballots are excluded. The LDPR ran as the Zhirinovsky Bloc. Independents won only constituency seats. Changes are the table's; "New" is shown as no change. The article cites Nohlen & Stöver and the University of Essex. No by-region table, so no region winners. The infobox's percentages are the CEC's, which also count invalid ballots (Communist Party 24.29%), and its vote counts differ slightly from the results table (Communist Party 16,195,569, Unity 15,548,707); the table's are used.

candidates.name: Russian Party of Pensioners for Social Justice

elections.notes: Held from 17 to 19 September 2021; the date is the last day. The lead says that, like prior Russian elections, it was not free and fair; the OSCE sent no observers. Seats are each party's total (225 party-list plus 225 constituency); votes and shares are the party-list vote. The CEC's national totals include votes cast in Crimea and Sevastopol (in the article's by-region table). 1,171,581 invalid ballots are excluded from the shares. Turnout is the infobox figure. Region winners are the party that won most constituency seats in each federal subject, from the article's seats-by-region table (the only by-region table); subjects with a tie are left out. The infobox's percentages are the CEC's, which also count invalid ballots (United Russia 49.82%).
